content:
Thomas Baird: Kicking off thread on route normalization for Usage Insights. We need a canonical `route_key` to aggregate cost by route+model without exploding cardinality. I’m drafting ADR but want consensus on rules + edge cases (dynamic paths, OpenAI-compat routes).

Logan Wright: +1. Biggest pain today is everyone emits “route” differently (raw path, handler name, sometimes full URL :/). For the dataset we need something stable + comparable across gateway + telemetry.

Chloe Martin: From console backend POV: we can live with “best effort” mapping, but we need deterministic rules so customers don’t see row churn week-to-week.

Nadia Rahman: Also needs to reconcile vs billing. If we bucket too aggressively (everything becomes /other) we lose usefulness. If we don’t bucket enough, we blow up warehouse + query perf. So: strict normalization + explicit fallback buckets.

Thomas Baird: Proposed core: `route_key = <HTTP_METHOD> <normalized_path_template>`.
Rules draft:
- lowercase method, uppercase display? (either is fine if consistent)
- normalize path:
  - lowercase
  - strip scheme/host if present
  - drop query string + fragment
  - collapse multiple slashes
  - strip trailing slash (except root)
  - decode percent-encoding then re-encode reserved? (open question)
  - template path params (uuids, numeric ids, ULIDs, base58-ish IDs)
  - cap segment length (e.g., >64 => `{param}`)
- If path doesn’t match known patterns and has high entropy segments, bucket to `/__other__`

Jada Williams: For percent decoding: careful. If we decode `%2F` we can change semantics (segment boundary). Suggest: do NOT decode reserved `/` and `?`. Probably safest: only decode unreserved (RFC3986) + then normalize case. But that’s a rabbit hole.

Logan Wright: +1, please don’t let encoding become a source of “two different routes”. We can treat path as opaque string after stripping query + host, then apply segment heuristics.

Dylan Brooks: We should keep customer-facing terminology as “endpoint” but internal as `route_key`. DevEx folks worried “route” implies express router patterns.

Alex Martinez: yep. Docs/tooltips will say “Endpoint (normalized)” with an info icon explaining how we template IDs. Internally do whatever.

Felix Schneider: For OpenAI compat endpoints, customers will absolutely expect:
- `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- `POST /v1/completions`
- `POST /v1/embeddings`
- `POST /v1/rerank` (ours)
- `GET /v1/models`
Also there are some odd ones:
- `GET /v1/files/{file_id}`
- `GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content`
- `DELETE /v1/files/{file_id}`
Even if low volume, they’ll show up.

Thomas Baird: Agree, those can be explicit allowlist patterns in the normalizer (fast path). Anything else uses heuristic templating.

Mei Lin: Can we align on whether we include API version in the key? `/v1/...` vs `/v2/...`.

Chloe Martin: I think yes, include it. If we later ship `/v2/chat/completions` it’s not the same endpoint for cost. But we might want an alternate “route_group” dimension later.

Nadia Rahman: Include version in route_key. We can add `route_family` later if PM wants rollups.

Thomas Baird: OK. Edge case: workspace/project scoped internal APIs like `/v1/workspaces/abc123/projects/def456/routes/...` (not public). Do we ever want them in Usage Insights? Probably no, but telemetry might see them if emitted at gateway.

Logan Wright: For the initiative, we’re focusing on inference routes (generation/embeddings/rerank) exposed in Redwood API + OpenAI compat. We should exclude control-plane paths from dataset or bucket them.

Jada Williams: Recommendation: allowlist inference base prefixes: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/rerank`, plus maybe `/v1/responses` if we add it. Everything else goes to `/__non_inference__` so totals still match billing but we don’t create noise.

Chloe Martin: +1 to a `__non_inference__` bucket for now. Console can hide by default behind “Show non-inference endpoints”.

Dylan Brooks: Please make sure we can still reconcile totals. If billing includes control-plane costs (hopefully not?) we should see them somewhere.

Nadia Rahman: Billing should only be inference usage, but there are “metering events” that get emitted in a few other places. Having a bucket is good for detecting leaks.

Thomas Baird: Dynamic path templating heuristics draft:
- Segment matches UUID v4: `{uuid}`
- Segment matches ULID: `{ulid}`
- Segment numeric (>= 4 digits?) => `{id}`
- Segment base64/base58-ish length>=16 => `{id}`
- Segment contains `.` and looks like filename? keep? (e.g., `model.bin` unlikely in routes)
- Segment length > 64 => `{param}`
- Also we should template known keywords: `org_`, `ws_`, `proj_` prefixes? (we have those in some internal ids)

Jada Williams: Please don’t over-template numeric segments blindly. `/v1/models/7b` isn’t an ID. For OpenAI compat, models are in request body not path. For files endpoints, `{file_id}` is alphanumeric with `file-` prefix. Suggest: pattern list for known endpoints > heuristics.

Felix Schneider: +1. Pattern-based for inference + files. Heuristics only as fallback.

Logan Wright: Another edge: “OpenAI compatible base URL” sometimes includes `/openai` prefix depending on how customers proxy. Do we normalize that away?

Thomas Baird: Good call. I’ve seen `/openai/v1/chat/completions` in staging. We could treat `/openai/v1/*` as equivalent to `/v1/*`.

Chloe Martin: We do have that in some deployments. If we don’t normalize it, those customers will see split rows and complain.

Nadia Rahman: But be careful: not everyone’s `/openai` is ours. However, since this is our gateway route, we can safely map our own compat prefix.

Jada Williams: Proposed rule: strip leading `/openai` if it’s exactly `/openai/v1/...` and only when host is our gateway. In telemetry events we don’t always have host though.

Logan Wright: Telemetry has `service` and `ingress` fields, not host. If `ingress == gateway` and `path startswith /openai/v1/`, we can rewrite.

Thomas Baird: OK.
What about method? Some customers use `GET` with query params for health checks etc. For inference it’s basically POST-only. But method included in key helps avoid collisions.

Mei Lin: Including method doubles cardinality for any weirdness but manageable. + it helps debugging.

Dylan Brooks: Console tables should probably display just the path (since method is almost always POST), but filter can include method if needed.

Alex Martinez: In docs, we can show “POST /v1/chat/completions” in examples. That’s fine.

Thomas Baird: Another question: do we normalize “route” based on the user-requested path or the internal handler path? E.g. gateway might rewrite `/v1/chat/completions` to `/internal/inference/chat`. We want user-facing.

Logan Wright: User-facing. In telemetry we should capture the original request path at ingress before rewrites. If we only have handler route, the customer sees nonsense.

Chloe Martin: +1. We also need this for “what changed?” insights. If route suddenly changes due to internal refactor, the time series breaks.

Nadia Rahman: This touches instrumentation. We need a consistent field in metering events: `request_route` = normalized at gateway at request time.

Thomas Baird: Yep, ENG-3813 is shared normalization library; ENG-3822 adds route tag to metering events.

Jada Williams: Please ensure we don’t bake language-specific normalization into random services. Make one lib + one canonical test corpus.

Felix Schneider: Can we capture a set of test cases now? I can contribute OpenAI compat + weird prefixes.

Thomas Baird: Draft test corpus (add more):
1) `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions?foo=bar` => `POST /v1/chat/completions`
2) `POST /openai/v1/chat/completions` (ingress=gateway) => `POST /v1/chat/completions`
3) `GET /v1/files/file-abc123/content` => `GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content`
4) `DELETE /v1/files/file-abc123` => `DELETE /v1/files/{file_id}`
5) `POST /v1/workspaces/ws_123/projects/proj_456/chat/completions` => `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects/{project_id}/chat/completions` (or bucket?)
6) `POST /v1/chat/completions/` => `POST /v1/chat/completions`
7) `POST ////v1///embeddings` => `POST /v1/embeddings`

Chloe Martin: For #5 I’d rather bucket to `POST /__non_inference__` unless we’re sure those are real customer-facing endpoints. That path looks like internal.

Logan Wright: Agree, bucket. We should not surface workspace ids in route keys anyway (even templated). Better to keep that dimension separate (workspace/project) in aggregation.

Nadia Rahman: +1. There’s a privacy angle: even templated, long multi-segment internal routes are noise + hint at internal architecture.

Thomas Baird: OK: allowlist inference endpoints; anything else `__non_inference__` (still includes method). So #5 => `POST /__non_inference__`.

Jada Williams: Also need a “missing route” bucket when telemetry has no path (older emitters). Something like `POST /__unknown__`.

Logan Wright: +1. That’s useful to track instrumentation rollout.

Felix Schneider: One more OpenAI edge: some SDKs hit `/v1/chat/completions` but with `X-OpenAI-Client` header and we route to different handler. Doesn’t matter; route_key stays same.

Dylan Brooks: For ADR, can we explicitly call out that route_key is not guaranteed 1:1 with handler, it’s a reporting dimension.

Thomas Baird: Yep.
Next: query string dropping is non-negotiable, right? Some customers pass `?model=...` on nonstandard proxies.

Chloe Martin: Drop. Model is a separate dimension already. Query strings are pure cardinality risk.

Nadia Rahman: Drop query. If someone relies on `?deployment=...` or something, that should be a tagged dimension (region/deployment mode) not route.

Alex Martinez: DevEx note: we’ll get “why are my custom endpoints not split?” questions. We should have a tooltip: “Endpoints are normalized and query params are ignored.”

Thomas Baird: Ok.
I’ll incorporate into ADR: 
- Canonical route_key definition
- Allowlist inference + OpenAI compat + files endpoints
- Rewrite `/openai/v1/*` => `/v1/*` when ingress=gateway
- Drop query/fragment
- Strip host/scheme
- Collapse slashes + strip trailing slash
- Bucket unknown/missing/non-inference
- Provide test corpus + required emit point (gateway)

Logan Wright: Please add a section on “why” (cardinality, stability, billing reconciliation) + explicit non-goals (not a general URL normalization library).

Jada Williams: Also include the exact bucket strings so they’re stable across services:
- `/__unknown__`
- `/__non_inference__`
- `/__other__` (if we keep it)
Make sure we don’t accidentally localize / rename them later.

Nadia Rahman: +1. Billing reconciliation job can alert if `__unknown__` exceeds X%.

Thomas Baird: Good point. I’ll set target: `__unknown__` < 0.5% of requests after rollout.

Chloe Martin: Once ADR is up, I’ll link in the console backend ticket so we can implement filters + labels consistently.

Felix Schneider: I’ll send a PR comment with more OpenAI route examples + file endpoints.

Alex Martinez: When ADR is ready, tag me — I’ll make sure wording aligns w/ docs (“endpoint normalization”).

Thomas Baird: Will do. Drafting now, will post in #eng-platform later today for final review.
